entries.note: al-Targhīb leaves two iḥtimālāt; Taṣḥīḥ al-Furūʿ corrects Ibn Mufliḥ's lead that on this premise she does not dispose. Against the reading's undemanded output.

evidence.excerpt_ar: المصنف قد قدم حكما وهو أنه يصح ولا يتصرف، وهذا الصحيح من المذهب.
evidence.note: On the view that the half does not enter the husband's ownership by force, al-Mardāwī says Ibn Mufliḥ put forward a ruling, «يصح ولا يتصرف», and that it is the correct view of the madhhab, against al-Targhīb's two wujūh; read as barring the wife's disposal.

entries.note: al-Qāḍī alone against Taqī al-Dīn; al-Buhūtī transmits Taqī al-Dīn's weakening without demur, so the support leans against the reading.

evidence.excerpt_ar: والذي ينبغي أن تسليم الموهوب إلى الموهوب له يذهب حيث يشاء، وإرسال
evidence.note: Under the matn's rule that ownership in the sick man's gift is held in suspense («مراعى»), al-Buhūtī quotes al-Ikhtiyārāt: al-Qāḍī's view that the donee takes and disposes is weak; the gift should not be handed over to go where he wills, but held so the heir can reject it after the death.

entries.note: al-Inṣāf and Ibn Mufliḥ correct non-liability and al-Iqnāʿ is decisive for it; the reading's liability side (ẓāhir al-Khiraqī) is marjūḥ. Residue: candidate farq, the buyer's planting by right in his own property.

evidence.excerpt_ar: الصحيح من المذهب. اختاره القاضي وغيره. قال في الفروع: لا يضمن نقص الأرض
evidence.note: If the buyer, owner of the plants, uproots them, he does not make good the land's loss on the correct view of the madhhab, chosen by al-Qāḍī; al-Kāfī is decisive, reasoning that he committed no transgression.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ولا يضمن نقصها بالقلع، في الأصح، فإن أبي أخذه الشفيع بقيمته حين تقويمه،
evidence.note: The buyer who planted before the shafīʿ learnt of his right may take his plants and does not make good the land's loss by uprooting, on the sounder view.

evidence.excerpt_ar: ذلك ولو مع ضرر ولا يضمن نقص الأرض ولا يلزمه تسوية حفرها
evidence.note: If the shafīʿ chooses to take and the buyer wants to uproot, he may, even with harm, and neither makes good the land's loss nor levels its holes.

evidence.excerpt_ar: وقيل: يلزمه. وهو ظاهر كلام الخرقي. ومال إليه الحارثي.
evidence.note: The contrary wajh, liability, is the apparent sense of al-Khiraqī and al-Ḥārithī inclines to it, saying the levelling of the holes goes with the arsh.
